paper_title: Exact Solution for Two δ-Interacting Bosons on a Ring in the Presence of a δ-Barrier: Asymmetric Bethe Ansatz for Spatially Odd States (Olshanii, 2025, SciPost Physics Core submission)
core_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
For a two-boson wavefunction satisfying bosonic exchange symmetry, oddness under point inversion about the barrier is equivalent to oddness under reflection about the mirror $x_1=-x_2$:
\[
\Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-\Psi(x_1,x_2)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Psi(-x_2,-x_1)=-\Psi(x_1,x_2).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad \Psi(x_2,x_1)=\Psi(x_1,x_2)\quad\text{for all }(x_1,x_2).\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad I(x_1,x_2):=(-x_1,-x_2).\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad S(x_1,x_2):=(x_2,x_1).\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad R(x_1,x_2):=(-x_2,-x_1).\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad R=S\circ I=I\circ S.\\
\text{(P6)}&\quad \text{Point-inversion oddness means }\Psi(I(x_1,x_2))=-\Psi(x_1,x_2).\\
\text{(P7)}&\quad \text{Mirror oddness means }\Psi(R(x_1,x_2))=-\Psi(x_1,x_2).
\end{aligned}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Assume point-inversion oddness. Then
\begin{align}
\Psi(R(x_1,x_2))
&=\Psi(S(I(x_1,x_2))) && \text{by (P5)}\\
&=\Psi(I(x_1,x_2)) && \text{by exchange symmetry (P1)}\\
&=-\Psi(x_1,x_2) && \text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
Thus mirror oddness holds. Conversely, assume mirror oddness. Then
\begin{align}
\Psi(I(x_1,x_2))
&=\Psi(S(R(x_1,x_2))) && \text{because }S\circ R=I\\
&=\Psi(R(x_1,x_2)) && \text{by exchange symmetry (P1)}\\
&=-\Psi(x_1,x_2) && \text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}
Thus point-inversion oddness holds.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-\Psi(x_1,x_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Psi(-x_2,-x_1)=-\Psi(x_1,x_2)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
